title: Grammar rule
description: One record in data/languages/<iso3>/grammar/<kind>.yaml. Field names and shape from SPEC.md §3.2: 'Grammar rule becomes {id, kind, lhs, rhs, conditions, comment, source}'. The archive's own rule syntax never separates a pattern from a condition on that pattern (docs/unl-reference/formats/transformation-grammar.md); conditions here starts empty, with everything on lhs, until issue 15 decides the split (flagged, not decided by this schema).

id.description: The rule's identifier: a catalogue number where the archive has one (M2, Y38), or an importer-assigned sequential id where it does not (T-rules and D-rules carry no number in the archive).

kind.description: Which grammar/<kind>.yaml file the rule belongs to. Not itself an archive field; the importer derives it from which export the rule came from.

lhs.description: The left-hand side (α) of the rule: the pattern the rule matches, exactly as the archive writes it, including any embedded conditions (negation ^, disjunction {a|b}) until issue 15 splits them out.

rhs.description: The right-hand side (β) of the rule: the rewrite the rule performs. Empty string for a rule shape that has no right side in the archive (e.g. a subcategorisation frame, which declares an argument structure, not a rewrite).

conditions.description: Conditions split out of lhs. Archive: embedded in lhs; the archive's own grammar syntax never separates them (docs/unl-reference/formats/transformation-grammar.md). The split policy is an open question for a rule-author (see docs/factory/store-schema.md); this array is empty until that question is resolved.

comment.description: What the rule does, in one line, in the writing voice (docs/standards/data.md). Archive: present as free trailing text after ';' for T-rules; absent per-line for M/Y catalogue entries, where the importer writes the comment from the paradigm's or frame's own catalogue description.

archive_path.description: Path under data/archive/ the record was read from.

line.description: Line number in archive_path, or a descriptive locator (e.g. a paradigm or frame catalogue number) when the archive export has no per-line grain.
